Rebelhorn × Cyberpunk 2077: What Makes These Motorcycle Jackets Different?
items.summary: What Sets the Rebelhorn × Cyberpunk 2077 Motorcycle Jackets Apart? The collection draws directly on Cyberpunk 2077 and the world …
items.content:
The collection draws directly on Cyberpunk 2077 and the world of The Night City, a futuristic metropolis where cybernetics, megacorporations, mercenaries, and street culture mix into something unmistakable. Rebelhorn translates that atmosphere into motorcycle apparel through a technical look, dark colorways, distinctive graphics, contrasting details and futuristic accents.

If you’ve ever walked the streets of The Night City as V, this style will feel instantly familiar. The jackets are designed to echo the neon-soaked urban world of the game while remaining genuine riding gear.

Looks are only the beginning. Like a merc’s gear before the next job in The Night City, a motorcycle jacket has to deliver when the road stops being predictable.

Cyberpunk 2077 is set in a futuristic world, but the Rebelhorn × Cyberpunk 2077 collection is built for real riders. That’s why its futuristic look goes hand in hand with essential motorcycle safety features, such as:

This is where the collection goes beyond style. Rebelhorn uses the world of Cyberpunk 2077 as its starting point, but turns that spirit into genuine motorcycle gear. The result is a jacket that can evoke the neon streets of The Night City without losing sight of its main purpose: protecting the rider.

You don’t have to live in The Night City to feel its energy from behind the handlebars. The Rebelhorn × Cyberpunk 2077 collection carries the look of the game’s world into real riding: city streets, night rides and long-distance routes.

Dark colorways, technical details and motifs from Cyberpunk 2077 evoke V’s world, where technology, individualism, and street style are part of everyday life. That makes the jacket more than a piece of riding gear. It’s a way to express your style and stand out on the road.

It’s this blend of an iconic universe and real-world function that makes Rebelhorn × Cyberpunk 2077 more than just a futuristic look. Likewise, it’s a way to take a piece of The Night City with you, beyond the screen.

Whether you ride daily or only on weekends, choose a jacket that fits well, matches your riding style and suits the conditions you face most often. Before buying, check the size chart, the protector levels and the materials used. That way, your gear can serve you well for many seasons, combining comfort, safety and a look inspired by the world of Cyberpunk 2077.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners' Showrunner Talked About Canon Ending Of Cyberpunk 2077
items.summary: Bartosz Sztybor also addressed whether Season 2 confirmed a female V as canon.
items.content:
Bartosz Sztybor also addressed whether Season 2 confirmed a female V as canon.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, the hugely popular Netflix anime by Studio Trigger set in CD Projekt Red's Cyberpunk 2077 universe, recently returned for its second season, which many fans watch with special attention, since it's set in 2078, just one year after the events of the game, and it has sparked fresh questions about how its story connects to the wider franchise. In a recent interview with IGN, showrunner Bartosz Sztybor addressed some of the biggest questions.

The supposed female V cameo in an Arasaka database, listed alongside other cyberware-compatible individuals, is one example fans have pointed to as a possible indication that V is canonically female and still in Night City sometime after the events of Cyberpunk 2077. According to Sztybor, such theories are ultimately just speculation: he stressed that the Cyberpunk franchise is built around "standalone stories that are self-sufficient." This is also why he isn't particularly concerned with including Easter eggs.

Cyberpunk: Edgerunners deliberately avoids establishing a canon ending for Cyberpunk 2077:

"We don't want to set a canon ending. So there were a lot of conversations again with the lore team to see what we can do to somehow satisfy all the endings, and what will be the state of the world after the game. That's why the scene that you asked about, we don't want to be straightforward, but we are giving some suggestions that will probably reveal the state of the world in more comic books and other stuff. So there are discussions. There are discussions, but we are not setting one kind of ending."

"There is canon, of course. But again, when we were creating Edgerunners 1 and multiple comic books and board games, the canon was before the game. So we knew the state of the world. And for the things post-game, it's not that there are super detailed canon things, but one important canon information is that Arasaka is weakened and that's it. And it gives us a lot of opportunities to show the city in a different way. But again, it's not detailed. So it doesn't make any of the endings canon. But the things that happened in the game could lead to that, whatever your choice was."

In the same interview, Sztybor also addressed the third season of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners. Although it launched six years ago, Cyberpunk 2077 continues to reach new heights, hitting the milestone of 40 million copies sold this summer. The franchise is also expanding with a live-action film adaptation and a sequel in development, with half of the quest team reportedly consisting of former modders.

items.title: CD Projekt RED Continues to Grow Development Teams With Warhorse Studios Veterans
items.summary: The recent additions to CD Projekt RED's teams include developers who have worked on Kingdom Come: Deliverance and its sequel.
items.content:
CD Projekt RED is continuing to grow its development teams while it keeps quietly working on The Witcher 4 and the sequel to Cyberpunk 2077 . As reported by GamesRadar , the latest additions to the studio are veterans of the RPG genre and include Karel Kolmann , who previously worked on both of the Kingdom Come: Deliverance games as a lead gameplay designer, and is now a senior quest designer at CD Projekt RED.

Joining Kolmann is former Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 lead level designer Zdeněk Glatz , who joined CD Projekt RED earlier this year as a senior open-world designer. Along with them, Warhorse Studios’ former lead technical designer Zbyněk Zelinka has now joined the Cyberpunk 2077 developer as a senior gameplay designer. Zelinka seems to be the latest addition to the team, having only joined last month following his tenure at Warhorse Studios that lasted over seven months.

CD Projekt RED pursuing industry veterans that have quite a bit of experience with RPGs that give players plenty of choices to make should come as no surprise. According to the studio’s joint CEO Adam Badwoski, The Witcher 4 will give players choices that will “leave a lasting impression.” The team has been putting an “immense focus” on the game’s narrative, and will have plenty of major emotional beats that will leave an impact on players.

In the meantime, CD Projekt RED has also been working on another secretive project dubbed Hadar . Just last month, co-CEO Michał Nowakowski spoke about how the team now has a “coherent vision” for the project, and that it is the studio’s “biggest undertaking to date.”

“It’s been the biggest undertaking so far that has taken us a few good years, but at this point we can say that we have a coherent vision of this world and its key elements. The team has started work on the game, although it is still not yet in pre-production,” he said (via machine translation). “Some small prototypes are currently being created, and gameplay elements are being tried.”

As for what Hadar will be, CD Projekt RED has been largely silent on the matter. However, a job listing has indicated that it will be an “emotional, open-world experience”. Nowakowski himself had spoken about development progress on the project back in March, and at the time, he said that “multiple prototypes” were in the works that would help set a proper vision for Hadar .

“Now, we have clearly defined distinguishing features of this world, and established key pillars that will not only provide the foundation for the game itself, but also, potentially, for other future products.”

As for CD Projekt RED’s larger ambitions, Nowakowski said back in June that the company has no plans to flood the market with constant releases . While big games might start coming out from the studio at some point on a yearly basis, he said that “this is not the goal.”

“We have a rough ten-year rolling plan, but the goal is not to flood the games market with CDPR games. We just want to make really cool games, and we don’t want to have a ton of IPs either. We’re not planning to grow in that way.”

Platforms: PS5, Xbox Series X, PS4, Xbox One, PC

items.title: 5 Open-World Games You Can Play for Months
items.summary: The best open-world games, like Cyberpunk 2077, have so much to do that players will enjoy them for months.
items.content:
Image via CD Projekt Red Add CBR on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover By Angelina Bonilla Published Nov 2, 2026, 9:45 PM EST Angelina is a librarian and writer who has been writing about video games since 2014. Her work has appeared in publications including GameSkinny and NoobFeed, as well as smaller publications like LT3. Angelina has interviewed Lindsey Stirling, Open Bionics and a number of independent game developers and content creators. She graduated from the Florida Institute of Technology with a BA in Humanities. Outside of writing, she enjoys anime, video games, literature, philosophy, and media studies. Sign in to your CBR account Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Listen Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Open-world games are massive by design, and because of that, it's easy for players to get lost in them. The best games in the genre encourage players to explore, and many titles have deep gameplay mechanics that allow players to approach the game's challenges in all kinds of ways.

Games like Cyberpunk 2077 and Skyrim are so vast that players can sink dozens of hours into them, even without mods. Many of these games give players a reason to replay them, even after they've reached the end credits, and players are still discovering new things about them years after their release.

Kingdoms of Amalur Re-Reckoning Battle Image via THQ Nordic Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning came out in February 2012, only a few months after Skyrim . With Bethesda's leviathan-like game dominating the public zeitgeist, Kingdoms of Amalur had to compete with one of the biggest RPGs of the generation for players' attention. However, Kingdoms of Amalur stood out thanks to the impressive creative pedigree behind its world.

R. A. Salvatore, best known for the Legend of Drizzt novels, served as the game's Executive Creator of Worlds, helping shape its setting and extensive lore. Ken Rolston, known for his work on The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind , served as one of the designers, while famed composer Grant Kirkhope, known for Banjo-Kazooie, co-created the game's score.

Rip Mystery Packs of Graded Cards & Collectibles

Japanese Pokémon Center 20th Anniversary Promo · PSA 10

Must be 18+/19+ to participate depending on jurisdiction.

One of Kingdoms of Amalur's most fascinating features is its unique leveling system. Called the Destiny system, it functions as the game's character class system, allowing players to specialize in Might, Finesse, or Sorcery, or combine them. Players can follow one path, combine two, or create a hybrid of all three, and they can freely change their Destiny throughout the game.

Then there is the combat, which may look like basic hack-and-slash gameplay at first, but becomes much more satisfying as players experiment with different weapons and abilities. All of these systems give Kingdoms of Amalur something that many open-world RPGs struggle to achieve: the freedom to experiment without punishing the player for changing their mind.

Wei Shen in Sleeping Dogs Definitive Edition Image via Square-Enix The spiritual successor to the True Crime series, Sleeping Dogs plays like any good undercover story, drawing comparisons to the hit 1985 Jackie Chan film Police Story. A former San Francisco police officer with a troubled past, Wei Shen, returns to his birthplace of Hong Kong and joins the police force. He then goes undercover to infiltrate the Sun On Yee Triad organization.

The game teaches players all of its mechanics before setting them loose in Hong Kong, where almost every corner of the city has something waiting for them. What makes Sleeping Dogs stand out is how it implements three different types of XP: Triad, Police, and Face. Triad XP is rewarded through melee combat, environmental kills, and complex attacks.

Sign in to claim your place on the leaderboard!

Face XP comes from the cosmetic items players obtain, including clothes and vehicles, while Police XP is earned by minimizing property damage and civilian casualties. Each type of XP provides its own benefits, although Triad and Police XP have more gameplay advantages, while Face XP is primarily cosmetic. These systems encourage players to approach each mission differently.

There are also plenty of collectibles, dateable women, races, gambling games, and other activities scattered throughout Hong Kong. While the main story remains linear, the city itself provides plenty of reasons to step away from it. Players can spend hours hunting down collectibles, upgrading Wei's abilities, exploring the city, or simply causing trouble on the streets.

items.title: 'The Dialogue That They're Having There Is Very Important' — Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 Showrunner on V Speculation, Canon Endings, and Building a Franchise Fans Love
items.summary: Edgerunners 2 showrunner Bartosz Sztybor on all things Cyberpunk, including V's apparent appearance, canon endings, and more.
items.content:
Edgerunners, the hugely popular Netflix anime set in CD Projekt’s Cyberpunk 2077 world, takes what’s great about the video game and expertly translates it into the world of animation. The recently released Season 2 told its own story — one we know is set just a year after the events of the main game , in 2078 (more on this later) — and it all wraps up nicely. But wait! Was that a tease for V in the show? And, if that’s true, does that mean there’s an ending of Cyberpunk 2077 that CD Projekt considers canon, and thus acts as the jumping off point for all post-game spinoffs like Edgerunners 2?

At the Lucca Comics & Games festival, we got the chance to put all this to Edgerunners writer, producer, and showrunner Bartosz Sztybor, who did his best to answer without giving much of the game away. And speaking of giving the game away, what about that Season 3?

The world of Cyberpunk is set to expand further, of course, with the in-development Cyberpunk 2 (where and when the game takes place is yet to be announced). There's also a live-action film in the works, although according to CD Projekt, the Cyberpunk 2077 movie won't retrace the game's steps .

IGN: Eagle-eyed fans spotted that in the scene in the data archive, there's a wall of images and there's one that looks like it may be female V. Was that intentional, or something left to interpretation?

Bartosz Sztybor: It's left for interpretation. But also the dialogue that they're having there is, I think, very important. So yeah, it's left for interpretation.

Yeah I ain’t crazy that’s deadass V https://t.co/3XC5KtlrDa

IGN: Easter eggs from the game, is that an important thing for you all to include?

Bartosz Sztybor: It's not important at all. That's why I wouldn't call it Easter eggs. I think that's the way we are trying to create a franchise for Cyberpunk. So, to create standalone stories that are self-sufficient, that you can just read one comic book and you are having the catharsis and you don't need to know any other comic book or a game or other stuff. But we are putting those things that are not as a fan service, but for the audience or the readers to feel that this world is alive. That's why we don't want to create anime or animation or a comic book that will need the audience to read three other comic books and two TV shows to understand why this guy is a villain. But I like to put those many things like Sal Bigelow in Edgerunners 2, who was what, five years earlier in the comic book Cyberpunk: Big City Dreams. But only if there’s a reason.

So it's never thinking that, oh, what we should put in this scene to make fans happy? It's about building a bigger narrative.

IGN: When you are setting something after the game, after 2077, do you have conversations with CDPR about a canon ending for the game, that would set up a world state for Edgerunners 2? Or is it more kind of abstract than that?

Bartosz Sztybor: It's both, I would say. It's not like super abstract, but also, we don't want to set a canon ending. So there were a lot of conversations again with the lore team to see what we can do to somehow satisfy all the endings, and what will be the state of the world after the game. That's why the scene that you asked about, we don't want to be straightforward, but we are giving some suggestions that will probably reveal the state of the world in more comic books and other stuff. So there are discussions. There are discussions, but we are not setting one kind of ending.

IGN: When you're writing these stories, do you have a set canon in mind, or is it a little bit more variable than that?

Bartosz Sztybor: There is canon, of course. But again, when we were creating Edgerunners 1 and multiple comic books and board games, the canon was before the game. So we knew the state of the world. And for the things post-game, it's not that there are super detailed canon things, but one important canon information is that Arasaka is weakened and that's it. And it gives us a lot of opportunities to show the city in a different way.

But again, it's not detailed. So it doesn't make any of the endings canon. But the things that happened in the game could lead to that, whatever your choice was.

items.title: From the Anime to the Game — Free Update Brings Edgerunners 2 Content and More to Cyberpunk 2077!
items.summary: The free Edgerunners 2 Update to Cyberpunk 2077 is available now, with content inspired by the second installment of the hit anime series now streaming on Netflix
items.content:
“Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2” premiered on Netflix on October 20, bringing a whole new cast of characters to Night City for a dark, gritty ride. And now we’re bringing a little piece of that story into Cyberpunk 2077 , too! The free Edgerunners 2 Update is here, with content inspired by the anime, new ways to fight, more customization options, and plenty of other additions.

We’ve got a lot to cover, so let’s get into it. And don’t worry if you haven’t watched the new anime yet — no “Edgerunners 2” spoilers ahead!

One of the things we love about Night City is that there’s always another story unfolding somewhere. V may be central to the events of Cyberpunk 2077 , but they’re hardly the only merc in town, fighting to survive and make a name for themselves on those neon-soaked streets. Every fixer has clients, every crew has gigs to take care of, every Night City merc has their story — and sometimes, those stories collide in unexpected ways.

That’s exactly what happens in the brand-new quest introduced with the “Edgerunners 2” Update. What begins as just another gig from Wakako turns into an action-packed, high-stakes mission that sees V cross paths with Weak Kingsley, a famed Night City merc and one of the main characters of “Edgerunners 2.” We won’t spoil what happens, but during the course of this mission, V has a chance to assist Weak and his crew during a risky gig that takes place in a brand-new location: Night City Prison.

The new “Edgerunners 2” gig is more than a chance to encounter characters from the anime in the game — it serves as a prequel to the events of the series. So, play the quest before watching the anime, and you’ll have a little extra context going into Episode 1. Already seen the show? Then with this gig, you’ll get to revisit part of Weak’s story with a broader perspective of him and his crew.

And there’s even more forEdgerunnersfans in this update. For starters, you can find and equip Weak’s full outfit — vest, glasses, coat, pants, the works — and get your hands on his signature revolver, Coronation. We’ve also added a new radio station, HKGN 102.FM, featuring official tracks from both “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Edgerunners 2.” So if you’re planning to spend a few more hours cruising around Night City after watching the show, we’ve got your soundtrack covered.

What’s better than blasting your way through a warehouse full of gangoons with a revolver, dealing one headshot after another? Doing it with two revolvers, obviously.

That’s right — dual wielding is here! With the Edgerunners 2 Update, you can raise hell with a pistol or revolver in each hand. That’s a whole new vibe — and a whole new level of awesome.

But dual wielding isn’t just about looking cool. It brings a new playstyle and a fresh way to approach combat — in fact, it’s one of the most significant gameplay additions to the game’s combat since Update 2.0 introduced throwing knives. So if you’ve been looking for an excuse to shake up your fighting style, this might just be it.

Cyberware enhances your stats and abilities — but what if it could take your style to the next level, too? That’s where glamdocs come in. These new vendors let you customize the appearance of your cyberware, with 40 styles in different colors to choose from. Fancy a new look for your chrome? Pay them a visit at one (or all) of the five locations across Night City and see what catches your eye.

In a city that lives and dies by appearances, V really can’t afford to pass up any opportunity to shake up their look. On top of cyberware customization, we’ve also added 20 new hairstyles and several clothing sets to give your V the best chance of standing out, even in Night City.

We know how creative the Cyberpunk 2077 community can be, and we’re always curious to see what players come up with. That’s why we’re introducing cross-platform mod support through mod.io integration.

The update adds a Mods panel where you can browse and install supported community-created content directly in the game. It’s a new way to experiment with your experience, and we’re looking forward to seeing how it develops as more mods become available and receive support over time!

We’ve covered some of the bigger additions, but there’s still plenty to find in the Edgerunners 2 Update.

Thought you were done with Night City? Well, Night City's not quite done with you!

Patch notes for Cyberpunk 2077's Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) are now available for your early perusal before the update hits the streets on October 22nd. Watch the Features Overview video to see some of the new features in action:

And if you want to know even more, read through the list of most important changes below:

Edgerunners Content

  • Added a new side quest, Clampdown, set before the events of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2. To unlock it, complete The Heist and two gigs for Wakako, then wait for a message from her.

    [/*]

  • Added a new 5-piece gear set based on the character King, which can be obtained during the Clampdown side quest.

    [/*]

  • Added a new radio station, HKGN 102.0 FM, featuring a selection of tracks from the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners series.

    [/*]

Show Off

  • A brand-new clothing collection has arrived in Night City! 5 new outfit sets can now be purchased from certain clothing vendors:

    • Maxiwear: available in Heywood, Arroyo, Little China

      [/*]

    • Jinguji: available in City Center

      [/*]

    • NetWatch: available in Kabuki, Japantown

      [/*]

    • IconAmerica: available in Pacifica, Badlands, Northside

      [/*]

    • And one more set that will hit Night City shelves just a little later...

      [/*]
    [/*]

  • The NUS Infiltrator clothing set can be now purchased from clothing vendors in Kabuki and Japantown.

    [/*]

  • 4 new TWINTONE skins for Quadra Turbo-R V-Tech are now available via Twitch Drops.

    [/*]

  • Some of the hairstyles that were previously exclusive to NPCs are now available for V. Please note that some hairstyles are available only to feminine or masculine body types.

    [/*]

  • Show off your chrome! You can now customize your hand cyberware. Equip your Mantis Blades, Gorilla Arms, Monowire or Projectile Launch System, and visit one of 5 Glamdocs (marked with a spray paint icon on the map) to give your implants a fresh, new look. Each Glamdoc is located in a unique shop, along with their own intro scene with voiceover and animations, and offers a unique catalog of cyberware skins with customizable colors.

    [/*]

  • Sometimes one gun just isn't enough. The new Double Trouble perk in the Cool tree (along with four auxiliary perks) introduces an entirely new playstyle, allowing you to dual-wield Pistols and Revolvers from the Power category.

    [/*]

  • Added frames from the Cyberpunk Trading Card Game to Photo Mode, allowing you to make your preem shots look like custom cards.

    [/*]

  • Added new poses in Photo Mode to show off your dual-wielding prowess.

    [/*]

Mod the World

Added Cross-Platform Mod Support, powered by mod.io, a first step into cross-platform modding that allows you to easily browse and install a selection of player-created mods directly from the in-game menu. More mods will become available over time. The feature is available on PC, Mac, PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro and Xbox Series X|S.

Upgrading the World

  • Welcome to Paradise! Added a new side quest that takes you on a journey to uncover a mystery and explore Night City on a guided tour narrated by Richard Night. It unlocks after completing The Heist and reaching level 15 Street Cred.

    [/*]

  • Added 12 new Minor Arcana Tarot Cards to discover across Night City. The Tarot menu now has separate sections for Major and Minor Arcana. The new tarot cards are part of a new side quest, an extension of Fool on the Hill, which activates after scanning any of the new cards. Collect them all to get a special reward.

Quality of Life

    [/*]

    [/*]

  • Modded saves in the "Load Game" menu are now marked with a dedicated icon. Please note that achievements and trophies cannot be earned while playing on console from a modded save file.

    [/*]

  • Updated the selection of AMD FSR options. FSR 3 upscaling is no longer included, while FSR 2.1, FSR 4, and FSR 3.1 Frame Generation remain available.

    [/*]

  • Updated the CD PROJEKT RED Account connection, My Rewards and telemetry consent menus.

    [/*]

Technology

  • Added support for DLSS 4.5, including up to 6X Multi Frame Generation or Dynamic Multi Frame Generation, and the 2nd Generation Transformer Model.

    [/*]

  • Added support for glasses-free 3D effects on compatible Samsung Odyssey 3D monitors, along with a Motion Comfort setting that lets you balance 3D depth and viewing comfort.

    [/*]

  • Added support for MetalFX Frame Interpolation on Mac.

    [/*]

  • Added a toggle in settings for FSR Anti-Lag 2.

    [/*]

  • Introduced various performance optimizations, including improvements specifically for Ray Tracing.

    [/*]

  • Improved HDR rendering to provide more accurate colors, brightness, and contrast on compatible displays.

    [/*]

Fixes

  • Things Done Changed- Fixed an issue where the Delamain cab could get stuck after crashing into another vehicle, blocking quest progression.

    [/*]

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where tagging enemies while scanning could also cause V to crouch or stand up when using certain control schemes.

    [/*]

    [/*]

Chrome up, chooms! A new, free update for Cyberpunk 2077 is coming on October 22nd. And it sounds like a perfect time for another REDstreams.

Join us this Wednesday, October 21st at 5 PM CEST for a closer look at Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) and some of its new features. We're talking cyberware customization, a new dual-wielding playstyle, and more!

Tune in on Twitch, YouTube or Steam:

A huge thank you to Taisei Uchida (Original Art), Yukiko Kakita (Ink & Paint Check), and Yuichiro Tozawa (Special Effects) for their contributions to the Cyberpunk 2077 Edgerunners 2 Update (2.5) official illustration.

items.content:
To survive in Night City, you need someone to watch your back. On the way to the major leagues, V managed to gather a remarkable crew. You could even say, a crew to remember!

From trusted allies to unforgettable personalities, these are the people who helped shape V’s journey through the City of Dreams. This episode of It’s All About You is dedicated to the legendary crew that stood by V through every high and low.

Thank you for staying with us and expressing your love for Cyberpunk 2077 in the most creative ways possible. Don’t forget to check out our gallery to see more works, and, of course, share your creations with us: http://cdpred.ly/AAY

See you in the next episode!

items.content:
Listen up, Samurai! 🤘🔥

Celebrate five years of Cyberpunk 2077 in this special anniversary episode of It’s All About You, looking back on Night City’s unforgettable stories through the legends and music you met along your journey!

Sure, the city’s full of noise — sirens, synths, gunfire in the distance — but if there’s one song that became its soul, it’s “Never Fade Away.”

We brought together legendary artists from across the city of dreams to reinterpret this iconic track — each in their own voice, their own style, their own rebellion. ❤️‍🔥

Plug in, turn it up, and dive into our latest It’s All About You episode.

Because legends don’t fade.
